subject: Request: PO Field Enforcement & Netterm Bundling for Northfield Pilot
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>

Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: PO Field Enforcement & Netterm Bundling for Northfield Pilot

Hi Liam —

Thanks again for the time on Tuesday. We're excited about the pilot with Northfield and want to make onboarding as smooth as possible for your AP and procurement teams. A couple of procurement items that came up during our internal review — can you confirm Northfield's requirements so we can map payment flows correctly?

Key asks from your side we need to reconcile:
- PO presence: Your AP requires a PO number on each invoice line item (not just the header). Is that strictly required for every consolidated invoice or only for invoices tied to different subsidiaries?
- Net terms: You mentioned net60 in the call. For budgeting reasons, our sales team is proposing net45 for the pilot in exchange for consolidating invoice cadence. Is net45 acceptable, or do you need to stick to net60?
- Invoice cadence & consolidation: Would Northfield consider a single monthly consolidated invoice that contains line-level PO references (and a master PO header)? If not, can we use a single master PO per legal entity and include subsidiary routing metadata?

I've attached the PO template you sent last week (Northfield_PO_template_v2.pdf) — reproduced here so we can mark required vs optional fields. If you can loop in AP (cc'ed) and confirm the exact fields they will reject vs tolerate, we can produce a mapping plan and updated invoice sample.

Goal: agree on a small set of acceptance rules we can bake into our billing engine, avoid weekly micro-invoices, and keep the pilot cashflow predictable for both sides.

Next steps: if AP confirms they need per-line PO enforcement, we will propose one of two options: (A) require distinct POs per subsidiary and send multiple entity invoices, or (B) accept a single master PO with line-level PO references in a supplemental field. We'll propose a trade — earlier payment (net45) in exchange for consolidated monthly billing and a single PO mapping approach.

Can AP confirm by EOD?

Thanks —

Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0123

Subject: Re: Request: PO Field Enforcement & Netterm Bundling for Northfield Pilot

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear write-up. Quick answers from procurement/AP perspective:

- PO requirement: AP requires a PO identifier on every invoice line when multiple internal cost centers are billed. If the invoice is purely for a single legal entity and references our master PO, AP will accept line items without separate PO numbers.
- Net terms: Standard is net60. We can make a one-off exception for pilots, but that requires Procurement sign-off and an internal approval ticket. Net45 is possible but not a default.
- Consolidation: We prefer a monthly consolidated invoice at month-end. The caveat: if the consolidated invoice spans multiple legal entities, AP will break it into separate payments unless each legal entity has its own PO or you supply an explicit entity mapping file.

For our internal processing, the minimum required fields are: PO Number (header or line-level), Invoice Date, Legal Entity (ERP code), and a Line Item Cost Center. If you can populate Legal Entity and Cost Center fields in your invoice export, AP will be able to route payments without requiring distinct invoices.

I'll need Procurement (Maya) to sign the net45 exception. Copying her here — Maya, can you confirm whether Procurement can approve net45 for a small pilot (deal NW-2026-0012) if Redwood provides consolidated monthly invoices and a mapping file?

Best,
Liam
Head of Procurement | Northfield Systems
liam.oconnor@northfield.io

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 13:30:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Request: PO Field Enforcement & Netterm Bundling for Northfield Pilot

Team — forwarding Northfield's response. TL;DR: they will accept consolidated monthly invoices for a single legal entity, but multi-entity invoices need explicit mapping or separate POs. Procurement will consider net45 with approval.

Suggested commercial workaround (so we don't lose deal velocity):
- Offer a mapping file approach: each invoice will include a master PO header and a CSV attachment that maps each line item to Northfield's ERP legal_entity and cost_center fields. This keeps a single monthly invoice but provides AP what they need.
- Commercial sweetener: offer a 1.5% early-pay discount if payment is moved to net30 for the pilot (limited to first 3 months). If they won't do net30, propose net45 in exchange for a small implementation fee credit (we can absorb up to 5% of MRR for pilot setup).

I've attached a quick pricing exceptions workbook to show impact to our unit economics. Ben/Kim — can you review the attached and confirm the most we can concede for a pilot while keeping expected CAC payback intact? I want a response back to Liam with concrete numbers by EOD.

Thanks —
Vanessa
VP, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-pricing-exceptions.xlsx (xlsx)

Liam / Maya / AP team —

Thanks for the quick clarifications. Based on Procurement's constraints, here's a concrete proposal to unblock the pilot with minimal operational friction:

What Redwood will deliver:
- Consolidated monthly invoice (month-end) per legal entity. If the pilot lives under one legal entity, we'll send one invoice. If multiple legal entities are involved, we'll still generate a single consolidated file but include an entity_mapping.csv attachment that lists invoice line -> ERP code.
- Invoice format: Master PO header (Master PO ID), line-level fields include Service Date, SKU, Quantity, Line Amount, Line PO (optional), Legal_Entity, Cost_Center. This satisfies AP routing rules.
- Billing terms: propose net45 for the pilot (deal NW-2026-0012). As discussed, Procurement to confirm via internal approval. If Northfield can move to net30 for the pilot, Redwood will provide a 1.5% early-pay credit on invoice total for the first 3 months.

Attached: updated PO template with our suggested mapping (Northfield_PO_template_v2.pdf - updated) and the pricing exceptions workbook Vanessa referenced (redwood-pricing-exceptions.xlsx).

Requested next steps:
1) Maya / Procurement: confirm whether you can approve net45 for NW-2026-0012 (or advise what minimal additional info you need).
2) AP: confirm the list of required file fields for automated ingestion (we'll mirror them exactly).
3) Jordan/Redwood: once AP confirms field set, we'll send a sample invoice + entity_mapping.csv before month-end for test ingestion.

If we can get sign-off on #1 and #2 by next Tuesday, we can start the pilot billing in October with a clean ingestion test on Sept 30.

Thanks again — appreciate the fast cycle here.

Best,
